data.sentence: Thanks everyone. The goal today is to decide whether we change Comply pricing before the Q3 price book locks at the end of the month.
Quick context: Comply v2 adoption is strong, but the per-report overage model is causing friction, and we're discounting heavily to win renewals.
From billing support, it's been rough. We've had nine overage disputes since the v2 launch, and Clearwater was the biggest at thirty-two hundred dollars.
Most of them are the same story — customers exploring on-demand reports with no idea there was a limit, and no in-app warning.
And that's the worst possible experience. The feature we're using to win people back after the outage is the one surprising them with a bill.
Agreed. The no-warning part is a bug for migrated accounts, and that fix ships next week. But the bigger question is the model itself.
From sales, the per-report model is hard to explain. Customers ask how many reports they'll need, and nobody knows.
Meanwhile, SentinelShield and VaultEdge both quote flat platform pricing. VaultEdge came in eighteen percent under us at Summit Trust.
And we've been giving Comply away for free in year one to save renewals — Bridgeport, Summit Trust, a few others.
Which worries me. If year one is free and year two has overages, we're setting up a second wave of disputes next spring.
So here's the proposal. Three tiers — Essentials, Professional and Enterprise — with unlimited on-demand reports in every tier.
The tiers differ by number of frameworks, auditor package exports and API access, not by report count.
Unlimited reports would be a much easier conversation. I can sell that tomorrow.
What happens to the customers already disputing overages?
We'd credit any overage charged since April seventh and move them onto the matching tier at renewal.
That's a strong story for Customer Success. It turns a complaint into a goodwill gesture.
What does it cost us? Overage revenue isn't nothing.
About a hundred and ten thousand a year in overage revenue goes away. Finance thinks we recover it if the Professional tier lifts the average deal by eight percent.
That's realistic if we bundle Professional with Protect. That's the combination customers keep asking for.
Careful with Protect, though. Engineering asked us to slow Protect onboarding until the scheduler fix is out.
Good point. We can launch the bundle in the price book but gate new Protect onboardings on the scheduler rollout.
One more thing from support — can we get usage visible in the console? Half our billing tickets are customers asking what they used.
Yes, a usage page is part of this. Even with unlimited reports, customers want to see seats and API calls.
I'd want an eighty percent usage alert on seats too. The Axiom invoice issue this week was another surprise bill.
Yeah, Axiom's first invoice on the elastic seat model was wrong, and they only signed in April. That's not a good look.
Okay, adding seat alerts. Let's decide: does anyone object to taking the three-tier model to the pricing committee?
No objection from sales.
Customer Success supports it.
Support supports it, especially the overage credit.
Great. I'll write it up with finance for the committee on the twentieth.
